::: {.lead}
**shinygen** turns a text prompt into a production-quality [Shiny](https://shiny.posit.co) dashboard — generated, screenshot-tested, and quality-scored — all inside an isolated Docker sandbox.
:::

---

## {{< fa star >}} Core Capabilities

::: {.feature-grid}

::: {.feature-card}
#### {{< fa robot >}} Multiple LLM Agents
Leverages **Claude Code** (via Anthropic), **Codex CLI** (via OpenAI), **Gemini CLI** (via Google), and **OpenCode** (via OpenCode Go) to autonomously write clean and professional app layouts.
:::
::: {.feature-card}
#### {{< fa brands docker >}} Docker Isolation
Generations run in isolated containers using [Inspect AI](https://inspect.ai-safety-institute.org.uk/), protecting your host system from side-effects.
:::

::: {.feature-card}
#### {{< fa camera-retro >}} Visual Self-Correction
The sandbox agent takes local Playwright screenshots, reviews layout rendering, and dynamically corrects visual styling before submission.
:::

::: {.feature-card}
#### {{< fa scale-balanced >}} Multi-Judge Evaluation
An external, host-side LLM panel scores code quality, visual design, functionality, and UX, feeding back critiques for refinement.
:::

::: {.feature-card}
#### {{< fa arrows-rotate >}} Iterative Refinement
Runs automated generate-judge-refine cycles until code meets the quality threshold, up to `--max-iterations`.
:::

::: {.feature-card}
#### {{< fa book >}} Custom Skills Injection
Pass custom guidelines and component directories to enforce branding rules, library preferences, and modern coding standards.
:::

::: {.feature-card}
#### {{< fa flask-vial >}} A/B Benchmark Arms
Compare treatment (`--skills`) vs control (`--no-skills`) to measure exactly how much your skill rules improve generation scores.
:::

::: {.feature-card}
#### {{< fa globe >}} Web Search Fetching
Allows agents to fetch up-to-date documentation and examples from the live web. Can be disabled with `--no-web-fetch`.
:::

:::

## {{< fa bolt >}} Installation & Requirements

### Quick Install

Install `shinygen` via pip in editable mode:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/karangathe/shinygen.git
cd shinygen
pip install -e .
```

If you plan to use screenshot-based visual evaluation and host-side verification, install the playwright extras:

```bash
pip install -e ".[screenshot]"
playwright install chromium
```

::: {.callout-tip}
Docker sandbox images containing R, Python, Playwright, and headless Chromium are pulled and built automatically on your first generation run.
:::

### System Prerequisites

Make sure the following dependencies are available on your system before running `shinygen`:

```{python}
#| echo: false
from great_tables import GT, md
import polars as pl

reqs = pl.DataFrame({
    "Requirement": ["Python", "Docker", "API Key"],
    "Details": ["3.10+ (Recommended: 3.12)", "Docker Desktop daemon running", "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, GEMINI_API_KEY, or OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY"],
})

(
    GT(reqs)
    .tab_header(title="System Prerequisites")
    .cols_align(align="left")
    .opt_stylize(style=1, color="blue")
    .tab_source_note(
        md("`export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY='sk-ant-...'`, `export OPENAI_API_KEY='sk-...'`, `export GEMINI_API_KEY='...'`, or `export OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY='sk-...'`")
    )
)
```

## {{< fa terminal >}} Quick Start Guide

You can run `shinygen` either through the CLI command `shinygen generate` or via the programmatic Python API.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Python Dashboard (CLI)

```bash
# Generate a Python-based Shiny app with Claude Sonnet
shinygen generate \
    --prompt "Create a sales dashboard with filters by region and product category" \
    --model claude-sonnet \
    --output ./my-dashboard
```

### R Dashboard (CLI)

```bash
# Generate an R-based Shiny app (shiny-r)
shinygen generate \
    --prompt "Create an interactive mtcars data explorer with ggplot2 charts" \
    --model claude-sonnet \
    --framework shiny-r \
    --output ./my-r-dashboard
```

### Programmatic API

```python
import shinygen

result = shinygen.generate(
    prompt="Create a clinical trials dashboard with enrollment trends",
    model="claude-sonnet",
    output_dir="./trials-app",
    framework="shiny-python",
    data_csv="./trials_data.csv",
    screenshot=True,
    judge_model="openai/gpt-5.6-luna",
    max_iterations=3,
)

print(f"Generated app path: {result.app_dir}")
print(f"Score: {result.score:.2f} (Passed: {result.passed})")
```

### Batch Generation

Evaluate multiple models or prompts sequentially. Create a JSON config file mapping jobs:

```{.json filename="batch.json"}
[
  {
    "prompt": "Create a clinical trials dashboard with enrollment trends",
    "model": "claude-sonnet",
    "output_dir": "./batch/sonnet",
    "csv_file": "./trials_data.csv",
    "screenshot": true,
    "judge_model": "openai/gpt-5.6-luna"
  },
  {
    "prompt": "Create a clinical trials dashboard with enrollment trends",
    "model": "gpt-5.6-luna",
    "output_dir": "./batch/gpt56",
    "csv_file": "./trials_data.csv",
    "screenshot": true,
    "judge_model": "openai/gpt-5.6-luna"
  }
]
```

Then run the batch config:

```bash
shinygen batch --config batch.json
```

:::

## {{< fa diagram-project >}} Architecture & Sandbox Deep Dive

### The Execution Loop

`shinygen` orchestrates a closed feedback loop: it runs the coding agent, spins up the application, takes screenshots, rates the visual output via an external LLM, and refines the code iteratively.

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-width: 9
%%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'themeVariables': { 'fontFamily': 'Inter, Arial, sans-serif'}}}%%
flowchart TD
    %% Color Palette Definitions
    classDef input fill:#e0f2fe,stroke:#0284c7,stroke-width:2px,color:#0c4a6e,border-radius:8px
    classDef core fill:#f1f5f9,stroke:#64748b,stroke-width:2px,color:#0f172a,border-radius:8px
    classDef agent fill:#f3e8ff,stroke:#9333ea,stroke-width:2px,color:#581c87,border-radius:8px
    classDef validation fill:#fef3c7,stroke:#d97706,stroke-width:2px,color:#78350f,border-radius:8px
    classDef judge fill:#ffe4e6,stroke:#e11d48,stroke-width:2px,color:#881337,border-radius:8px
    classDef output fill:#dcfce7,stroke:#16a34a,stroke-width:2px,color:#14532d,border-radius:8px

    A["👤 User Request<br/>(Prompt + Dataset + Flags)"]:::input --> B["shinygen API / CLI"]:::core
    
    B --> C["Start Iteration Loop"]:::core
    
    subgraph Sandbox["Docker Sandbox Execution"]
        direction TB
        C --> D["Inject Framework Skills & Context"]:::agent
        D --> E["LLM Agent Writes Code<br/>(Claude Code / Codex / OpenCode Go)"]:::agent
    end
    
    E --> F["Host-side Runtime Validation<br/>(Unconditionally Starts App & Captures Logs)"]:::validation
    
    F --> G{"Screenshots<br/>Enabled?"}:::validation
    G -- Yes --> H["Host Playwright Captures UI"]:::validation
    G -- No --> I{"Judge Model<br/>Enabled?"}:::judge
    H --> I
    
    I -- Yes --> J["LLM Judge Panel Evaluates<br/>(Scores Code + Visuals 1-10)"]:::judge
    J --> K{"Meets Quality<br/>Threshold?"}:::judge
    
    I -- No --> L{"App Started<br/>Successfully?"}:::validation
    
    K -- No --> M["Construct Refinement Feedback<br/>(Judge Critiques + Server Error Logs)"]:::core
    L -- No --> M
    M --> C
    
    K -- Yes --> N["✅ Save Artifacts<br/>(Code, Logs, Screenshots, Summary)"]:::output
    L -- Yes --> N
```

### Docker Sandboxing Mechanics

Every generation job occurs inside an isolated Docker sandbox managed via **Inspect AI**.
- **Images Used**:
  - Python: `ghcr.io/karangattu/shinygen-sandbox-python:latest`
  - R: `ghcr.io/karangattu/shinygen-sandbox-r:latest`
- **Isolation Boundaries**: The agent cannot see or modify files on your host machine. It can only read and write inside `/home/user/project` inside the container.
- **Auto-dependency Installation**: On startup, `shinygen` executes the framework's install command (`pip install ...` or `install.packages(...)`) to ensure all necessary rendering and plotting libraries (like `plotly`, `bslib`, `faicons`, `ggplot2`) are hot-loaded in the sandbox.
- **Web Search**: The agent has internet access to look up API docs and download styling examples. Disable this by passing `--no-web-fetch` (which blocks the web search tool).

## {{< fa camera-retro >}} Visual QA & Validation

### Hands-on Agent Self-Evaluation

When `--screenshot` is enabled, the sandbox agent leverages the **`visual-qa`** skill:
1. The agent starts the Shiny app inside the container as a background daemon (using `nohup ... &`).
2. It runs `screenshot_helper.py` to capture a Playwright screenshot on `http://localhost:8000`. By default, it pauses for **7 seconds** (configurable) to allow JavaScript/charts to load completely.
3. The agent reviews the screenshot, identifies design flaws (e.g., overlapping text, unstyled charts, missing headers), modifies the code, and takes another screenshot until it is satisfied.
4. It terminates the background daemon before submitting the final draft.

### Host-Side Verification & Logging

Once the agent completes its run, `shinygen` performs a host-side runtime check:
- It launches the app on the host machine using a dynamically allocated free port (validated range `1-65535`).
- It captures startup logs. If the app crashes on launch, `shinygen` catches the traceback and feeds it directly into the next iteration's refinement prompt.
- It takes host-side Playwright screenshots to pass to the external LLM judge.

---

## {{< fa scale-balanced >}} Quality Evaluation & Value-Based Scoring

### Multi-Judge Panel

If `--judge-model` is specified, `shinygen` routes code and host-side screenshots to an external LLM judge (or a panel of judges, if the flag is repeated). 

::: {.callout-note}
## Judge Validation & Retries
The judge model must be fully qualified starting with `anthropic/`, `openai/`, or `google/` (e.g., `openai/gpt-5.6-luna`). Unknown model providers will raise validation errors. Judge calls use automatic retry with exponential backoff (up to 3 attempts) for robustness against rate limits.
:::

The judges evaluate the dashboard across **four strict criteria**:

1. **Requirement Fidelity**: Does the app implement all requested tabs, charts, filters, and datasets?
2. **Code Maintainability**: Is the code modular, DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself), cleanly formatted, and easy to modify?
3. **Visual & UX Quality**: Evaluates human-perceived visual quality from rendered screenshots — whether the dashboard looks clear, useful, cohesive, trustworthy, and complete at first glance. Key standards include:
   - **One-Screen Usefulness (5-Second Rule)**: The landing view must immediately communicate the subject, 3–4 concise KPIs, a prominent primary visualization, and an actionable analytical story. Extra tabs add depth but cannot repair a weak first impression.
   - **Render-State Gate**: Visible screenshot evidence overrides code intent. Repeated empty cards, stuck spinners, tiny placeholder marks, or unresolved outputs cap `visual_ux_quality` at **3** even when surrounding chrome is polished.
   - **Layout & Structure**: Consistent grid alignment, comfortable spacing, and clear visual hierarchy (primary KPIs prominent, secondary views subordinated) without wasted whitespace or cramped tiles.
   - **Typography & Color**: Refined type scales (distinct header, section, body, caption weights), readable line-height, restrained color palettes (2–4 semantic accents), and high-contrast elements (WCAG AA).
   - **Component & Chart Legibility**: Grouped controls with clear labels, value boxes with meaningful icons/units/deltas, zebra-striped tables with aligned numerics, and charts with explicit titles, labeled axes, units, and restrained palettes (no default plotly rainbow or raw unstyled axes).
   - **State Polish & Graceful Errors**: Handled empty and loading states without raw tracebacks or broken layouts across viewports.
4. **Code Robustness**: Graceful error handling (no raw tracebacks visible to users), empty states handled cleanly, and stable reactive bindings.

### Visual & UX Quality Calibration Scale

```{python}
#| echo: false
from great_tables import GT, md
import polars as pl

rubric = pl.DataFrame({
    "Score": ["1–3", "4", "5", "6", "7", "8", "9", "10"],
    "Assessment": [
        "Broken, loading, or repeatedly empty visible outputs.",
        "Confusing, cramped, patchwork, or substantially incomplete dashboard.",
        "Mixed visual hierarchy, awkward density, weak chart choice, or poor coherence.",
        "Tidy but basic, sparse, weakly prioritized, or visually generic (typical default layout).",
        "Clear, trustworthy dashboard with strong information density and legible charts.",
        "Strong professional composition, coherent palette, polished components, and immediately useful landing view.",
        "Exceptional human favorite: cohesive, information-rich, beautifully styled, and complete.",
        "Essentially unreachable (flawless in every dimension with zero possible improvement)."
    ],
})

(
    GT(rubric)
    .tab_header(title="Visual & UX Quality Judge Rubric")
    .cols_align(align="left")
    .opt_stylize(style=1, color="blue")
)
```

### Value-Based Scoring Formula

Instead of raw quality alone, `shinygen` optimizes for **value-adjusted scores** to penalize wasteful API calls:

$$\text{value\_score} = \text{quality\_score} - \text{iteration\_penalty} - \text{cost\_penalty}$$

Where:
- **Iteration Penalty**: Deducts $0.35$ for each extra generation iteration.
- **Cost Penalty**: Deducts $1.00$ per $\$1.00$ of API generation cost (capped at a maximum deduction of $2.50$).

This formula ensures models that get the dashboard right in the first iteration at lower costs score higher than models that take many expensive correction steps.

## {{< fa book >}} Custom Skills Injection & A/B Benchmarks

### Injecting Custom Skills

"Skills" represent styling guides, code templates, and coding standards injected into the agent's workspace.
- **Standard Skills**: `shinygen` dynamically fetches the official app-authoring skills at runtime and caches the latest successful download: `shiny-for-python` from [`posit-dev/py-shiny`](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shiny/tree/main/shiny/.agents/skills/shiny-for-python) and `shiny-for-r` from [`rstudio/shiny`](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/tree/main/inst/skills/shiny-for-r). Set `SHINYGEN_PY_SHINY_SKILL_REF` or `SHINYGEN_R_SHINY_SKILL_REF` to use specific tags or commits instead of `main`.
- **Custom Skills**: You can inject your own guidelines (e.g. company styling themes, database query layers) using `--skills-dir <path>`.

### Creating a Custom Skill Directory

To write your own skill, create a folder with the following structure:

```
my-custom-skills/
├── SKILL.md                 # REQUIRED: Contains skill description and YAML frontmatter
└── references/              # OPTIONAL: Supporting markdown guides
    ├── cards.md
    └── theming.md
```

Your `SKILL.md` must start with a YAML frontmatter block:

```yaml
---
name: corporate-theme-skill
description: Guidelines for styling dashboards using the corporate HSL color palette.
metadata:
  version: "1.0"
---

# Corporate Styling Guidelines
- Use CSS variables for color branding.
- Avoid absolute positioning.
```

Inject your custom skill using:

```bash
shinygen generate --prompt "Sales App" --skills-dir ./my-custom-skills/
```

### Control vs Treatment Arms (A/B Testing)

You can benchmark skill effectiveness using the control/treatment flags:
- **Treatment Arm (`--skills`)**: Injects the framework skill plus any custom skills.
- **Control Arm (`--no-skills`)**: Bypasses skill loading entirely. The agent receives only the raw prompt.

`shinygen` tracks the arm used (`skills` or `vanilla`) inside the resulting `run_summary.json` to calculate the lift in quality score.

## {{< fa microchip >}} Model Ecosystem

### Model Types

`shinygen` routes across three distinct tiers of LLMs:

1. **Frontier Models**: Run in Docker containers (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI).
2. **OpenCode Go Models**: Routed via the OpenCode agent in Docker containers. API calls are authenticated using `OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY` and target `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1`.
3. **Local Models via LM Studio**: Run unmetered local evaluations (e.g., `gemma-4-26b-a4b` or `qwen3.6-27b`):
   - Runs **entirely on the host** (Docker check is bypassed).
   - Bypasses API key verification.
   - Sets pricing to **$0.00** so value-based scores are not penalized by token usage.
   - Targets the local server on `http://localhost:1234/v1` (configurable via `LMSTUDIO_BASE_URL`).

## {{< fa clip >}} Environment Variables

Set the following variables in your terminal or a `.env` file at the project root to authenticate:

| Environment Variable | Purpose | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | Authenticate Anthropic models (e.g. Claude Sonnet/Opus) | `export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY='sk-ant-...'` |
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` | Authenticate OpenAI models (e.g. GPT-5.6) | `export OPENAI_API_KEY='sk-...'` |
| `GEMINI_API_KEY` | Authenticate Google Gemini models (e.g. Gemini 3.7 Flash) | `export GEMINI_API_KEY='AIzaSy...'` |
| `OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY` | Authenticate OpenCode Go models | `export OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY='sk-...'` |
| `LMSTUDIO_BASE_URL` | Base URL endpoint for local LM Studio servers | `export LMSTUDIO_BASE_URL='http://localhost:1234/v1'` |

We maintain a complete suite of unit tests. Run them locally to verify sandbox configurations, config parsers, and API bindings:

```bash
# Install development dependencies
pip install -e ".[dev]"

# Run tests
pytest
```

## {{< fa comments >}} DashSwipe: Interactive Dashboard User Testing

To help align dashboard styles, this repository includes **DashSwipe**, an interactive user-testing survey application located in the [user_testing_app/](user_testing_app/) directory.

- **Purpose**: Collects human feedback on LLM-generated layouts. It serves screenshots anonymously, lets users tier-rank layouts (S/A/B/C/D/F), prompts for 2-word critiques, and writes evaluation statistics directly to a Supabase database.
- **Run Locally**:
  ```bash
  python3 -m http.server 8080 --directory user_testing_app
  ```
  Open **[http://localhost:8080/](http://localhost:8080/)** in your browser.
- **Database Schema**: Refer to [user_testing_app/README.md](user_testing_app/README.md) to set up the Postgres schema.
